question: Should ClawHub accept this publisher follow notification feature as part of the current follow stack, and should it wait for the base follow API and controls PRs to land first?
rationale: The PR adds new user-visible notification behavior over private follow state and publication safety decisions, which automation cannot approve without maintainer intent and runtime proof.

options.title: Fix and prove after the stack lands
options.body: Require the base follow API and controls PRs to clear first, then rebase this branch, fix the release visibility gate, and add real runtime proof before merge.

options.title: Review the full stack together
options.body: Maintain the stacked PRs as one feature rollout, but explicitly own the private follow-state and notification-boundary decision across the whole stack.

options.title: Pause the notification slice
options.body: Keep this PR draft or close/reopen later if maintainers do not want publisher follow notifications in core yet.

recommendation.title: Fix and prove after the stack lands
recommendation.body: Require the base follow API and controls PRs to clear first, then rebase this branch, fix the release visibility gate, and add real runtime proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen has the strongest current-main history across the publish paths, schema routes, and retention areas this PR extends.
